Matt's leadership style is centered around empathy, clarity, and empowering his teams to take ownership of their work. This approach involved organizing non-punitive post-mortems to learn from mistakes, fostering an environment of open communication, and pushing decision-making to those closest to the work.

Matt also implemented a 'permit to fail' culture, encouraging experimentation and innovation. This mindset enabled teams to pivot quickly and shorten project timelines, ultimately leading to higher-quality solutions that aligned more closely with client needs. His focus on decentralized decision-making and empowering teams resulted in increased engagement and satisfaction, contributing to improved retention and long-term project stability.

At **JP Morgan Chase**, Matt played a pivotal role in building the payment engine behind the ACCESS Next Generation platform. The project was driven by the need to accommodate **135,000+** clients across **180+** countries, each requiring bespoke payment modules beyond the capabilities of the out-of-box solution from Bottomline Technologies. Matt led a team of over **40** engineers and was embedded at Bottomline's Portsmouth offices to design and deliver these custom modules, including ACH, wire, FX/cross-border, and EFTPS tax payments. At **RBC**, Matt tackled the challenges of managing cross-border payments and FX transactions due to fragmented systems and manual processes. He designed end-to-end cross-border payment workflows, integrating real-time FX tools and automated alerts, which closed a competitive gap and improved SLA compliance for time-sensitive transactions. His work provided a complete implementation blueprint for **RBC**'s modernization efforts, equipping business clients to independently manage multi-currency accounts.
